Essential vocabulary

Conjecture, proof, counterexample

Conjecture

Conjecture

Say your own definition, then click.

A precise mathematical claim whose truth has not yet been established.

Proof

Proof

Say your own definition, then click.

A valid argument covering every case allowed by the assumptions.

Counterexample

Counterexample

Say your own definition, then click.

One allowed case that makes a universal claim false.

New bound

New bound

Say your own definition, then click.

A sharper limit, even when the exact answer remains unknown.

The asymmetry: many confirming examples do not prove a universal statement, but one valid exception refutes it.

Activity · 2 minutes

A convincing pattern?

n² + n + 41

For n = 0, 1, 2, 3 the outputs are 41, 43, 47, 53. All are prime.

Would 1,000 successful tests prove this always produces a prime?

Predict what happens at n = 40 before you press the button.

AI × Mathematics · Week 9A07 / 40

Interactive: Press “Test n = 0…39” first: all 40 values are prime. Collect predictions, then “Test n = 40”.

Let pairs discuss before revealing the next slide. The question about 1,000 successful tests is hypothetical. It does not assert this expression actually passes 1,000 tests. The nonnegative integer domain is intended.

Activity reveal

One exception settles the claim

At n = 40

40² + 40 + 41 = 1,681 = 41². The output is composite.

1,681 = 41 × 41

The lesson

Search can find the decisive example. Exact arithmetic checks whether it works.

Photo: Benjamin le Roux / Unsplash

AI × Mathematics · Week 9A08 / 40

Answer: the proposed universal statement is false. The counterexample does not make the earlier prime values disappear. It changes what we may logically infer from them.

Research workflow

The roles AI can play

01

Explore

Search for examples, useful lemmas, or promising constructions.

02

Connect

Suggest a technique from another mathematical field.

03

Argue

Produce a proof candidate that people and tools can examine.

04

Formalize

Translate a precise statement and proof into a proof assistant.

AI × Mathematics · Week 9A09 / 40

Interactive: “Next step” highlights each role with a real example from the lecture.

These roles can occur in different systems or within one workflow. Calling the whole process autonomous can hide the choices of problem, tools, and verification made by humans.

What counts as progress?

Research and benchmarks

A benchmark

Measures performance on a defined set of tasks under a stated protocol.

A research result

Adds something new to mathematical knowledge, with a precise claim and supporting argument.

A hard test score can be informative without settling an open problem, and one discovery does not prove broad reliability.

Sort each item

A model scores 35 of 42 points on an Olympiad paper.A defined task set and protocol: a benchmark.
A new superexponential lower bound for multicolor Ramsey numbers.New mathematical knowledge with a precise claim: a research result.
A system passes 6 of 10 unpublished questions under a grading protocol.Still a benchmark: performance on stated tasks, scored by a protocol.
An explicit polynomial counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture in 3D.It settles a previously open question: a research result.

AI × Mathematics · Week 9A10 / 40

Interactive: Students call out Benchmark or Research for each item before you click.

Original conceptual distinction. A difficult test score can be informative without settling a previously open problem. Conversely, one research discovery does not establish broad reliability on every mathematical task.

A new construction challenges a longstanding prediction.

Unit-distance conjecture

A surprising connection

The reported result

For infinitely many n, the construction has at least n1+δ unit-distance pairs for a fixed δ > 0.

Why it is interesting

Ideas from algebraic number theory enter a problem about ordinary planar geometry.

Simple grids give only a constant number of pairs per point. The conjecture said you could never do much better; the construction’s pairs-per-point keeps growing.

Toy arrangements for intuition — not the May 2026 construction

AI × Mathematics · Week 9A12 / 40

Interactive: Switch arrangements: a line gives about 1 pair per point, a square grid about 2, a triangular grid about 3. The new construction beats every constant.

OpenAI announced the result in May. Human follow-up work analyzes and develops the connection. The stated asymptotic result refutes the conjectured n^(1+o(1)) ceiling. Photograph: Yanir Rubinstein at a blackboard, from UMD Mathematics. It is contextual, not an image of the discovery.

July 2026

The Jacobian conjecture

Can a polynomial transformation be reversible near every point, yet fail to be reversible globally?

Fable AI helped find a counterexample in three complex dimensions.

Photo: lynying Ju / Unsplash
AI × Mathematics · Week 9A13 / 40

Tao’s July 21 exposition credits a counterexample found using Fable AI. Local invertibility means nearby information is recoverable. Global invertibility requires a single inverse across the whole domain. The staircase is only a visual analogy.

https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/07/21/a-digestion-of-the-jacobian-conjecture-counterexample/

Photo: lynying Ju. https://unsplash.com/photos/white-spiral-staircase-with-white-metal-railings-HqGeVrgV_ZY. Unsplash License: https://unsplash.com/license. Cropped to fit.

Jacobian · core idea

Local information can miss a collision

Local reversibility

A nonzero constant Jacobian guarantees local reversibility.

Global reversibility

Two different inputs reaching one output defeat a global inverse.

The counterexample satisfies the local condition and still has a collision.

Analogy: wrapping a line around a circle. Not the actual polynomial.

AI × Mathematics · Week 9A14 / 40

Interactive: Drag past 2π: every small step stays reversible, yet two inputs end at one output. That is the local-versus-global gap.

For the displayed polynomial in Tao’s exposition, det DF = −2 and distinct triples share the image (−1/4,0,0). This is an algebraic check, not a statement based only on numerical sampling.

https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/07/21/a-digestion-of-the-jacobian-conjecture-counterexample/

Jacobian · scope

The dimension matters

Three dimensions and higher

Refuted

A counterexample exists, so the general conjecture is false.

Two dimensions

Still open

A counterexample in three variables does not automatically settle the two-variable case.

Headline check

What crucial qualifier would you add to a news headline?

State the dimension, or say explicitly “the general conjecture”. Gao’s follow-up preprint gives constructions in every dimension greater than two; the two-dimensional problem remains distinct.
AI × Mathematics · Week 9A15 / 40

Expected answer: state the dimension or explicitly say the general conjecture. Gao’s follow-up preprint gives constructions in every dimension greater than two. Keep the two-dimensional problem distinct.

Astra · geometry

Sphere packing: limits on density

The question

How tightly can equal balls fill a space without overlap?

The advance

A sharper asymptotic upper bound in high dimensions reaches the Cohn–Elkies threshold.

An upper bound says “no arrangement can beat this”. It does not hand you the densest arrangement.

Two dimensions, where the answer is known. In high dimensions it is not.

AI × Mathematics · Week 9A18 / 40

Interactive: Toggle the two packings. In 2D the hexagonal packing is provably best; in high dimensions only bounds are known.

The result concerns the high-dimensional exponent and the power of a bounding method. It does not give the exact densest arrangement in every dimension. The fruit photograph offers a familiar three-dimensional analogy.

Astra · abstract algebra

Groups and their representations

Groups

Mathematical objects that describe composable transformations.

Non-sofic

A construction escapes approximation by finite permutations.

Connes

Different groups can have the same associated operator algebra.

Significance

A familiar representation can lose information about the original object.

The group-theoretic and operator-algebraic results answer separate questions. These short descriptions give the conceptual stakes, not the technical constructions.

Astra · Erdős problem 183

Ramsey theory: unavoidable patterns

The question

Color every link between points. How large can the set be before one color must contain a triangle?

The advance

A new lower bound grows superexponentially with the number of colors.

With two colors the answer is known: 5 points can avoid a one-color triangle, 6 points never can. Try it.

AI × Mathematics · Week 9A20 / 40

Interactive: Let a volunteer color K5 with no one-color triangle (pentagon one color, star the other). Then switch to 6 points: every coloring fails, so R(3,3) = 6. The Astra result is about many colors.

A lower bound demonstrates that avoiding a monochromatic triangle is possible up to a certain size. It is distinct from an exact Ramsey number. The colors in the photograph are contextual.

A public candidate disproof

Graffiti conjecture 6

α(G) ≥ r(G) + ln ρ(G)
α
Maximum size of a set of vertices with no edges inside it (independence number).
r
Graph radius: from the best “center”, how far the farthest vertex is.
ρ
Minimum number of disjoint paths covering all vertices (path cover number).

A public AI-generated counterexample remains a candidate result.

AI × Mathematics · Week 9A22 / 40

The conjecture dates to 2002. The record consulted was added August 17, 2026 and names GPT-5.6 Thinking with Jackson as prompter. The supplied July date was not established by this record. Do not describe it as refereed.

https://probxiv.com/problems/graffiti-conjecture-6

https://github.com/Lamptypeshi/graffiti-conjecture-6-counterexample

Graffiti · reported construction

A small inequality can refute a conjecture

5 < 4 + ln 3 ≈ 5.099

The smallest reported tree has independence number 5, radius 4, path-cover number 3.

The inequality is easy to check. The graph properties need their own proof — check them yourself.

AI × Mathematics · Week 9A23 / 40

Interactive: Students click vertices to find 5 with no edge between them (e.g. v0, v2, v4, v6, b). Then show radius and path cover. 5 is less than 4 + ln 3, so the inequality fails for this tree.

The s=0 tree is a path v0,...,v7 with additional leaves at v2 and v5. The record gives α=5, r=4, ρ=3, violating the proposed α≥r+lnρ inequality. Keep the candidate status visible. An AI checking its own work is not independent review.

https://probxiv.com/problems/graffiti-conjecture-6

The Millennium Problem

What can happen to a smooth flow?

Smooth at the start

Velocity varies smoothly across space, with no initial mathematical blowup.

Finite-time singularity

The equations predict unbounded velocity after a finite time in the proposed construction.

A singularity in the idealized equations is not a claim that real water moves infinitely fast.

Photo: Jeffrey Eisen / Unsplash

AI × Mathematics · Week 9A25 / 40

The continuum equations idealize fluids. A singularity in that model is not an assertion that real water literally travels infinitely fast. Existence in weaker mathematical senses is a separate issue.

https://www.claymath.org/millennium/navier-stokes-equation/

Navier–Stokes · assumptions matter

The exact scope of the announced result

Three dimensions
Incompressible fluid with positive viscosity.
Smooth forcing
The construction starts from rest and applies a smooth external force.
Bounded energy
Kinetic energy stays bounded while peak velocity becomes unbounded.
Important limit
This does not establish blowup for the unforced Navier–Stokes problem.
AI × Mathematics · Week 9A26 / 40

The paper’s Theorem 1.1 specifies a smooth force compactly supported in space and time and a velocity singularity as time approaches 1. OpenAI connects this to statements C and D of the official prize formulation.

Navier–Stokes · different questions

Proof checking and prize recognition

Manuscript

Does the written argument establish the precise theorem?

Formal artifact

Does the checked code encode the intended statement and assumptions?

Community review

Can independent experts understand, reproduce, and build on it?

Clay Prize

Qualifying publication, at least two years, and general acceptance are required.

Check yourself

Clay still lists the problem as active. Does that mean the proof has been found wrong?

No. Clay’s status follows its own process — publication, two years, general acceptance. OpenAI says it does not intend to claim the prize. An announcement is not an award decision, and neither is a verdict on correctness.
AI × Mathematics · Week 9A28 / 40

Clay’s page still labels the problem active as of the check date. OpenAI states it does not intend to claim the prize. A release announcement should not be confused with a Clay award decision.

Credit and responsibility

Attribution

Which earlier ideas and people made the result possible?

Transparency

Can others inspect how AI contributed to the argument?

Understanding

Access

Vote · who should answer for an error in an AI-generated proof?

The Leiden Declaration and AGMAI guidance frame these as questions about the health of mathematical research. Correctness does not by itself settle authorship, access, or incentives. Ask students which responsibility belongs to a lab, a researcher, or a journal.

The AI can propose. A small logical kernel checks the proof term.

Lean · strengths and limits

The trust boundary in a formal proof

Statement
The code must express the theorem people intend to prove.
Proof term
The kernel checks each construction against the formal rules.
Assumptions
Axioms and dependencies must be explicit and appropriate.
Interpretation
People assess meaning, novelty, importance, and correspondence to the problem.

A proof of a weaker or mistranslated statement may compile perfectly.

AI × Mathematics · Week 9A31 / 40

A proof of a weaker or mistranslated statement may compile perfectly. Formal checking is powerful, but it does not perform literature review or decide whether the theorem is valuable. Inspect placeholder proofs and unexpected axioms.

https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/Axioms-and-Computation/

https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/

Formal verification · toy example

A tiny Lean proof

What it says
For every natural number n, adding zero returns n. Here the equality follows from Lean’s definition of addition.
Why the second fails
Two statements a reader sees as “obviously the same” can need very different proofs. The kernel accepts only what it can check.
A research formalization scales this precision to thousands of definitions and lemmas. Responses are simulated for teaching.

Public and checkable
Release precise statements, clear proofs, attribution, and formalization status.

The independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence says members receive no company payment and it has no decision-making power at labs. Its guidance also asks labs to stop testing advanced problems on proprietary models. It is advice, not a certification of all announced proofs. The photograph illustrates discussion and does not show the advisory group.

AI-assisted inquiry
A workflow students can use
01
State
Write the exact claim and its allowed cases.
02
Challenge
Ask for counterexamples, missing assumptions, and prior work.
03
Check
Use exact calculations, independent reasoning, or a suitable proof assistant.
04
Explain
Write what you understand and credit both human and AI contributions.
AI × Mathematics · Week 9A36 / 40
Original classroom workflow. For a short assignment, ask students to submit an initial claim, AI interaction excerpt, one independent check, and a revised statement. Respect the course’s AI-use and collaboration policies.
Group activity · 4 minutes
Which headline would you publish?
Choose the defensible headline. Then rewrite the other two.
AI × Mathematics · Week 9A37 / 40
Answer: B is the most precise, with a date and review-status qualifier where space permits. A expands one mathematical theorem into all fluid problems. C confuses a company aggregate report with per-result verification. Ask groups to name the missing evidence.

Synthesis
What has changed?
Discovery
AI systems now contribute candidate arguments and explicit constructions.
Verification
Formal artifacts make some kinds of checking more reproducible.
Human work
Explanation, attribution, and independent review remain central.
Your habit
Read the exact theorem, the assumptions, and the evidence together.
AI × Mathematics · Week 9A38 / 40
Invite students to revisit the opening poll. The lesson should preserve both the scale of recent progress and the distinctions among a company report, a public proof, and a result that the community has absorbed.
